summary: Terra Mystica is a dense, no-luck engine-building and territory game where you terraform hexes to expand your faction's network while racing up four cult tracks for efficiency bonuses. Every turn is a tight optimization puzzle with heavy opportunity cost, and the game rewards players who plan several turns ahead over a fixed number of rounds.
praised: Deep, satisfying strategic depth with no luck or hidden information
Highly asymmetric factions that each play very differently
Elegant scoring/bonus tile system that gives replayability
Tight resource economy where every decision has real opportunity cost
criticised: Steep learning curve and heavy rulebook/upfront teaching burden
Low direct interaction beyond spatial blocking, can feel solitaire-ish
Some factions are considered stronger than others depending on map/matchup
Long playtime and analysis paralysis, especially with new players

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via terraforming adjacency, indirect competition for cult track and bonus positions

scoring.why: Points accumulate continuously from building, terraforming, cult track advancement, and end-game bonus tiles, so the winner is decided by consistent efficiency across many small scoring streams rather than one dominant strategy
